sections.h2: Start by finding out who bills your house
sections.html:
Ramapo is a patchwork of overlapping governments. Before you list, find out which of them bills and permits your house, settle the tax and certificate questions early, and pick a buyer who can close without waiting on a lender. The first step matters because the town holds a dozen incorporated villages and several hamlets, and each village collects its own taxes.

Ramapo lies in Rockland County, with New Jersey to the south and Orange County to the west. The mid-2025 estimate is 161,564 residents, 8.5% above the 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $653,100, and the average household has nearly four people, so extra space is in demand.

The villages are Airmont, Chestnut Ridge, Hillburn, Kaser, Montebello, New Hempstead, New Square, Pomona, Sloatsburg, Spring Valley, Suffern and Wesley Hills. Monsey, Viola, Hillcrest, Tallman and Sterlington are hamlets, not villages. Which one your street belongs to decides who sends the tax bills and who issues permits.

  • Suffern Central School District serves the western part of town.
  • East Ramapo Central School District serves the east, including Spring Valley, Monsey, Pomona, Chestnut Ridge and New Hempstead.

The district on your parcel decides which school tax bill a buyer inherits, so name it correctly in the listing and on the disclosure form.

Buyers will compare your house with these numbers, so it helps to know them before you set a price.

With households this large, additions and converted basements are common, and they are the usual reason a certificate of occupancy question comes up. Listing materials in more than one language can also widen your pool of buyers, since 59.0% of residents aged five and older speak another language at home.

sections.h2: Who collects tax, and how it plays out at closing
sections.html:
The Town of Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, but not for the villages. Each village bills and collects separately, so a house in Airmont or Suffern has a village bill that the town does not handle.

  • County and town tax may be split into four installments for a 5% service charge. The town takes the first by January 31, and the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance collects installments 2 through 4.
  • School tax cannot be split, because the Receiver does not take partial payments on the school bill.
  • Penalties begin in October for school taxes and in February for county and town taxes.
  • Under Real Property Tax Law section 922, a bill that never arrived does not excuse lateness.

The Receiver advises anyone about to sell to skip the installment plan. It adds 5% of the bill and can muddy the closing, where the seller is credited for the unused part of the taxes. The tax office at (845) 357-5100 can supply a payoff or a tax history, and your attorney should check village bills on their own. Owners who pay off a mortgage should send the satisfaction letter to both the town and village tax offices so later bills reach the right address.

sections.h2: If a tax bill looks wrong or a payment runs late
sections.html:
An error on a bill goes to the Town of Ramapo Assessor first. The Receiver cannot change a bill alone, and a corrected one is issued only after signed Correction to the Tax Roll paperwork comes back from the Rockland County Real Property Tax Department.

Timing is strict. Only an official U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of payment date, and a meter stamp does not. Checks sent through a bank's bill pay often carry no postmark, so the payment must actually arrive by the due date. Credit and debit cards work online only, with a third-party processing fee. Penalties are fixed by state law, and the Receiver cannot waive them for any reason.

Before closing, settle these points so a payment does not cross the title date: confirm what has been paid, ask whether any installment remains open, and get the school, county and town figures in writing for your attorney.

sections.h2: What to check with the Building Department
sections.html:
Building, Planning and Zoning reviews permits and supports the Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals. Its page carries forms that matter for unusual properties.

  • A list of required inspections for one- and two-family dwellings, which shows the steps a permitted project must pass.
  • A Certificate of Use application.
  • A Secondary Dwelling application, for a second unit on the property.
  • A Plumbing Test Certification form.

An online Property Search tool is also available. Use it with the permit application package to compare the town's file against what stands on the lot. After a basement conversion, a new kitchen or an addition, confirm a certificate of occupancy exists, because buyers' attorneys ask and New York's disclosure form puts the same question to the seller. The department's phone is (845) 357-5100.

The Rockland County Clerk receives the deed along with the TP-584 transfer tax return and the RP-5217 transfer report. The county sets recording fees, so ask the clerk for the current amounts, and ask your attorney when the TP-584 must be filed.

The state transfer tax is two dollars per $500 of price, rounded upward, and the seller usually pays it. A buyer of a residence at a million dollars or more pays a further 1% mansion tax.

The disclosure form carries its own duty. A seller of a house with up to four dwelling units signs it and delivers it ahead of a binding contract. If you later learn something that makes the form inaccurate, a revised copy is due as soon as practicable, though never after title transfers or the buyer moves in, whichever comes first.

sections.h2: A short checklist for Ramapo sellers
sections.html:
Start with the tax bills: identify the village, school district, town, county and any open installment. Then pull the certificate of occupancy and permits for every addition, finished basement or second unit. Next, decide how you want to sell. A listing reaches the widest group of buyers but depends on a buyer's mortgage and on lawyers on both sides. A cash sale leaves out the lender, the appraisal and the financing contingency, so the date depends mostly on title and paperwork.

Either way, the closing attorney will want the tax history, the disclosure form and the deed information together before the closing date is set.

faqs.q: Will the Town of Ramapo's tax office bill my village taxes?
faqs.a: No. Each village bills and collects separately, so a house inside a village has a village bill on top of the town, county and school bills.

faqs.q: Is Ramapo's installment plan a good idea before a sale?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver of Taxes advises against it, since it adds a 5% charge and can cause problems at closing.

faqs.q: How do I tell which school district my Ramapo house belongs to?
faqs.a: The west, including Suffern, Montebello, Airmont, Sloatsburg and Hillburn, is mainly Suffern Central, and the east is East Ramapo Central. Confirm against your school tax bill.

faqs.q: How is the state transfer tax figured on a Ramapo sale?
faqs.a: It is two dollars per $500 of the price, rounded up, and the seller usually pays it. Ask your attorney to confirm who pays under your contract.

faqs.q: How do I learn whether my Ramapo house has a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: Try the town's Property Search tool first, then confirm with the Building Department by phone at (845) 357-5100.
